Since 2017

Ashgill is a hill farm that grew a wood. Tom and Ellen Ridley planted the larches in 1994. The six pitches are far enough apart that you hear the river before your neighbours.

Open March to OctoberDogs welcome in two tentsFirewood included

Dark skies

Turn the lantern
off and look up.

We sit inside the Northumberland International Dark Sky Park. On a clear night the Milky Way is visible from your door. Binoculars and a star chart are in the barn.

  • The Perseids, peaking around 12 August
  • Saturn, when its seasonal position allows
  • Andromeda, a smudge with the naked eye

Sky visibility depends on weather, moonlight and the date. Check a current sky chart before your stay.

Getting here

A little further.
Worth the track.

Ashgill is two miles off the A68, the last half mile on a farm track that any car can manage slowly. Hexham station is forty minutes away, Friday pickups at 17:00 for £25.
